line: Lantern night. Ruth Hale and I are doing Diwali lanterns at the library. Kids from here, kids from her homework club, one table, far too much glue.
If it's here, only our kids come. If it's there, everybody's kids come, and ours get to be the experts for an evening. They stand up straighter.
Mr. Deshpande does. Anil thinks lanterns waste a Saturday. I think a kid who explains Diwali to his soccer friends is learning what both of them want.
One of my students translated his dad's lease. Twelve years old. They got the security deposit back. I gave him extra credit.
I'm borrowing the big tables for Thursday. Ruth says yes to everything. It's slightly alarming.
You're who the youth program needs. Not a teacher. Someone who moves between both rooms without making a speech about it.
